subject: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?

messages.author: a867c5b77d7f1de1
messages.subject: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?
parts:
Sometimes it is helpful to make some simple simulations and checks before running full model (and before compiling the code), so it would be helpful if Stan distribution functions could be called from R directly (yes, R has it's own but not all of them and there are slight differences in UI) - is it possible? My questions are:

Is it possible to call Stan distribution from R, e.g. using Rcpp as a proxy?
Are there any examples of this that can be found online?

Greetings,
Tim

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?
parts:
On Wednesday, July 15, 2015 at 5:36:00 PM UTC-4, Tim wrote:
Is it possible to call Stan distribution from R, e.g. using Rcpp as a proxy?
Yes
Are there any examples of this that can be found online?

No because it does not officially exist yet. If you can wait a few days for RStan 2.7.0, then skip step 1
  1. Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/R/expose_stan_functions.R to your working directory and comment out the line toward the end that says "#include <src/stan/lang/rethrow_located.hpp>"
  2. Write a .stan function like this:
    functions {
      real foo_log    (/* arguments, see chapter of user manual on User-Defined Functions */) {
            return(normal_log(y, 0, 1)); // for example
          }
    }
    model     {}
  3. Source the aforementioned expose_stan_functions.R file, call expose_stan_functions(), and then call foo_log() from R with whatever arguments it takes.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?
parts:
Neat!

Is there any interest in having the Stan functions built in rather than require
user coding? Writing a function like that will give you one instantiation
of the normal_log signature --- it doesn't actually expose all gazillion
instantiations (vector, row vector, array of double, int, double if
we don't care about autodiff, for all arguments, making a total of 5^3
or 125 possible instantiations). There may also be a matrix version for
normal --- not sure.

If this approach is good enough, my own inclination is to not clutter up
RStan with more functions.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?
parts:
On Wednesday, July 15, 2015 at 9:26:39 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
If this approach is good enough, my own inclination is to not clutter up
RStan with more functions.

People ask about the Stan densities (and the prngs) from time to time but I'm not inclined to maintain permanent R functions that expose parts of the Stan Math Library (where do you draw the line?) when using expose_stan_functions (the function formerly known as testify) is so easy and (knock on wood) not overly brittle.

Ben

messages.author: a867c5b77d7f1de1
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Calling Stan distributions from R - is it possible?
parts:
Thank you all for responses! I am waiting to see new version of Stan released!

As about making R equivalents for Stan functions - I also do not think it would be good idea to pack R=rstan with a function for each distribution. I would rather think of single function to call multiple distribution functions (e.g. pstan(), qstan(), rstan(), dstan()).

Greetings,
Tim
